page.excerpt: SKIP TO MAIN CONTENT SIGN IN CREATE ACCOUNT Samuel Langhorne Clemens Male 30 November 1835–21 April 1910 • LZJ1-TLQ Brief Life History of Samuel Langhorne When Samuel Langhorne Clemens was born on 30 November 1835, in Florida, Monroe, Missouri, United States, his father, Judge John Marshall Clemens, was 37 and his mother, Jane Casey Lampton, was 32. He married Olivia Louise Langdon in February 1870, in Elmira, Chemung, New York, United States. They were the parents of at least 1 son and 3 daughters. He lived in Buffalo, Erie, New York, United States in 1870 and Hartford, Hartford, Connecticut, United States for about 20 years. He registered for military service in 1861. His occupation is listed as compositor in New York City, New York, United States. He died on 21 April 1910, in Redding, Fairfield, Connecticut, United States, at the age of 74, and was buried in Woodlawn Cemetery, Elmira, Chemung, New York, United States. Samuel Langhorne Clemens, known by the pen name Mark Twain, was an American writer, humorist and essayist. He was praised as the "greatest humorist the United States has produced," with William Faulkner calling him "the father of American literature." His novels include The Adventures of Tom Sawyer (1876) and its sequel, Adventures of Huckleberry Finn (1884), with the latter often called the "Great American Novel."
